items.heading: HR Is Not Shrinking,
items.text: HR is not shrinking, and it is not the "soft skill filler job" some career forums still describe. It sits at the center of every hiring decision, every pay decision, and every exit decision a company makes, and none of that goes away as companies grow, whatever tools they adopt along the way.

items.heading: Strip Away the Title
items.text: Strip away the title and HR's core job is this: you make or influence decisions about people, who gets hired, who gets paid what, who gets trained, who gets let go, and you have to defend those decisions to people who often disagree with you.

rows: Non-MBA HR Executive, any bachelor's degree
Rs 2-3.5 LPA at most small and mid-size private employers
The most common entry door. A generalist degree plus decent communication and basic spreadsheet or HRIS familiarity is enough to get shortlisted for the bulk of India's entry-level HR openings.
A real bump over the non-MBA entry point, but not a dramatic one. The degree mainly speeds up the later move into HRBP or manager-level work, more than it changes the first offer.
MBA-HR from a premier B-school (XLRI, TISS, SCMHRD, MDI and similar)
This is where the credential genuinely reshapes the starting number, because these campuses run dedicated corporate HR placement pipelines most other MBA-HR programmes cannot access.
No formal HR degree, career switch into recruitment or L&D
Typically resets to entry-level pay for the first 6-18 months
Genuinely possible with transferable proof, running a team, handling vendor negotiation, or documenting process, but expect the pay to reset before it climbs on HR-specific merit.

items.heading: One Camp Pictures HR As
items.text: One camp pictures HR as steady, people-facing, always-in-demand work with a reasonable path to a senior title. That picture is broadly true for someone who specialises.

items.heading: The Other Camp Pictures HR
items.text: The other camp pictures HR as thankless paperwork, policy enforcement, and being the messenger for decisions someone else made. That picture is also true, for the entry-level layer of nearly every HR job.

items.heading: A Third, Newer Worry Has
items.text: A third, newer worry has entered the conversation fast: that AI screening tools are quietly making the recruiter and administrative side of HR obsolete. That worry is partly right, aimed at the correct layer of the job, but wrong about the function disappearing entirely.
